# ghost_release_asset (Resource)

Uploads a file to a release in a Ghost repository, as a release asset.

The content comes from exactly one of `file`, `content` or `content_base64`. The provider hashes it at plan time (`content_sha256`), so changing the bytes replaces the asset (Ghost can't change an asset's content in place). Renaming the asset or changing its label is done in place.

Ghost rejects empty files, accepts files up to 2 GiB on the public instance, and counts assets against the repository owner's storage quota. Assets of a draft release are visible only to people who can write to the repository. Deleting the release deletes its assets.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ghost_repository" "example" {
  name      = "example"
  auto_init = true
}

resource "ghost_release" "v1" {
  repository = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  tag_name   = "v1.0.0"
}

# A build output uploaded from a local file. The file is hashed at plan time,
# so a new build replaces the asset.
resource "ghost_release_asset" "linux" {
  repository   = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  release_id   = ghost_release.v1.release_id
  name         = "example-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
  label        = "Linux (x86_64)"
  content_type = "application/gzip"
  file         = "${path.module}/dist/example-linux-amd64.tar.gz"

  # Replacing the repository deletes its releases and their assets.
  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [ghost_repository.example.repo_id]
  }
}

# Small text content inline.
resource "ghost_release_asset" "checksums" {
  repository   = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  release_id   = ghost_release.v1.release_id
  name         = "SHA256SUMS"
  content_type = "text/plain"
  content      = "${ghost_release_asset.linux.content_sha256}  example-linux-amd64.tar.gz\n"
}

# Binary content, base64-encoded.
resource "ghost_release_asset" "icon" {
  repository     = ghost_repository.example.full_name
  release_id     = ghost_release.v1.release_id
  name           = "icon.png"
  content_type   = "image/png"
  content_base64 = filebase64("${path.module}/icon.png")
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The file name the asset is downloaded under, up to 255 characters, unique within the release. Names are case-sensitive, and can't contain `/`, `\` or control characters, start or end with whitespace, or be `.` or `..`. Changing it renames the asset in place, which changes `browser_download_url`.
- `release_id` (Number) The numeric ID of the release, e.g. `ghost_release.example.release_id`. Changing it forces a new asset.
- `repository` (String) The repository's full name, `owner/slug`, e.g. `ghost_repository.example.full_name`. Renaming the repository updates this in place; pointing it at a different repository forces a new asset.

### Optional

- `content` (String) The asset's content as a UTF-8 string, which is stored in state. Prefer `file` for anything large. Conflicts with `file` and `content_base64`.
- `content_base64` (String) The asset's content, base64-encoded, for binary data, e.g. `filebase64("dist/app.zip")`. It is stored in state; prefer `file` for anything large. Conflicts with `file` and `content`.
- `content_type` (String) The media type the asset is served with, e.g. `application/gzip`, without parameters such as `charset` (Ghost drops them). Defaults to `application/octet-stream`. Changing it forces a new asset.
- `file` (String) The path of a local file to upload. It is read at plan time to work out `content_sha256`, so a changed file replaces the asset. A file that doesn't exist yet at plan time (one created during the apply) is read at apply time. Conflicts with `content` and `content_base64`.
- `label` (String) A short description the web UI shows instead of the file name, up to 255 characters. Changed in place; `""` and null both mean no label.

### Read-Only

- `asset_id` (Number) The numeric asset ID.
- `browser_download_url` (String) The download link in the web UI, `…/releases/download/<tag>/<name>`. Anyone who can read the repository can use it once the release is published.
- `content_sha256` (String) The hex SHA-256 of the content. A change replaces the asset. After import it is computed by downloading the asset.
- `created_at` (String) When the asset was uploaded.
- `download_count` (Number) How many times the asset has been downloaded, as of the last refresh.
- `id` (String) The repository's full name and the numeric asset ID, `owner/slug:asset_id`.
- `node_id` (String) The GraphQL node ID.
- `repository_id` (Number) The numeric ID of `repository`.
- `size` (Number) The size of the asset in bytes.
- `updated_at` (String) When the asset was last changed. Ghost also bumps it when the asset is downloaded, along with `download_count`.
- `url` (String) The asset's API URL. Ask it for `application/octet-stream` to download the content.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Release assets are imported by the repository's full name and the numeric
# asset ID, "owner/slug:asset_id". The import downloads the asset once to work
# out content_sha256. Set content_type in the configuration to the imported
# asset's type, or the default (application/octet-stream) replaces it.
terraform import ghost_release_asset.linux my-user/example:456
```
